# RASD-Health: the watchdogs

A rule that is not fed looks exactly like a rule on a quiet day. These searches keep watch over the chain under every detection - sensor, forwarder, index, fields, schedule - and each row they return names the detections it blinds. They are generated from what the library's own rules read, so a new detection is watched from the build that adds it. [How it works](../../docs/HEALTH.md).

| Watchdog | Runs | Fires when | Splunk | Sentinel |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **silent** | hourly | A host that reported in most hours of the past week has sent nothing on a channel for four hours. | [`silent.spl`](spl/silent.spl) | [`silent.kql`](kql/silent.kql) |
| **volume** | daily | A host sent, in the last day, none or under a quarter of what it sent on the same day a week earlier, of an event the rules read. | [`volume.spl`](spl/volume.spl) | [`volume.kql`](kql/volume.kql) |
| **fields** | daily | A field the rules read is filled in under 95% of the events that should carry it. | [`fields.spl`](spl/fields.spl) | [`fields.kql`](kql/fields.kql) |
| **delay** | hourly | Events indexed in the last hour arrived later than the scheduled searches wait. | [`delay.spl`](spl/delay.spl) | [`delay.kql`](kql/delay.kql) |
| **schedule** | hourly | A scheduled detection search did not run, or was skipped. | [`schedule.spl`](spl/schedule.spl) | [`schedule.kql`](kql/schedule.kql) |

The Splunk app schedules the five SPL searches as `RASD Health - <name>` and writes each row to the alert index as `sourcetype=rasd:health`. The KQL searches are for Sentinel analytics rules or a workbook; `schedule.kql` reads the `SentinelHealth` table, which health monitoring has to be turned on for.

> **Run on a live Splunk, in the lab.** The table is what Splunk Enterprise 10.4.5 answered when each SPL search was run once beside 3 lab hosts, after the attack steps ([kept runs](../../purple/lab_runs/README.md); the record is each part's `siem-searches.json`). It shows that Splunk accepts the searches as generated, and what they return over a lab that is in order: a row there would be a false alarm. It does not show a watchdog catching its fault. No feed was broken on purpose, and `silent` and `volume` compare with a week that a host made for one run has not lived. The KQL searches have not run on a live Sentinel.

| Watchdog | `hosted-45453509158/lab-linux` | `hosted-45453509158/lab-web` | `hosted-45453509158/lab-windows` |
|---|---|---|---|
| **silent** | ran: 0 rows | ran: 0 rows | ran: 0 rows |
| **volume** | ran: 0 rows | ran: 0 rows | ran: 0 rows |

## The same watch, on an export

No SIEM is needed to ask the question: `rasd health` compares an export of today's telemetry with a baseline and gives every detection a verdict.

```bash
rasd health --sample                                         # three ordinary days, then the day the pipeline breaks
rasd health last-week.jsonl --save-baseline health-baseline.json
rasd health today.jsonl --baseline health-baseline.json --scheduler scheduler.jsonl
```

On the bundled sample (`samples/health`: a baseline of 3.0 d from 8 hosts, then a day in which the pipeline breaks in several places without a sound), **4 detections are blind and 13 degraded**, 4 healthy, 1 with nothing to compare:

| Check | What broke | Blind | Degraded |
|---|---|---|---|
| **silent** | process_access: every host that sent it is silent (ws01, ws02, ws03, ws04 still send other events, and none of this kind); the baseline saw about 99 events over the same hours | `T1003.001_lsass_memory_access` | - |
| **fields** | field CommandLine is in none of 91 events (the baseline filled it in 100%): the same events now carry command_line | `T1053.003_crontab_noninteractive_install`<br>`T1059.004_linux_suspicious_shell_execution` | - |
| **schedule** | no run of 'RASD - T1190_object_id_enumeration' in the scheduler's record | `T1190_object_id_enumeration` | - |
| **silent** | process_creation: 1 of 4 hosts silent (ws03 still sends other events, and none of this kind since 2026-11-06 10:11); the baseline saw about 32 events over the same hours | - | `T1021.006_wsmprovhost_suspicious_child`<br>`T1053.005_powershell_scheduled_task_creation`<br>`T1053.005_schtasks_suspicious_creation`<br>`T1059.001_powershell_encoded_command`<br>`T1218.011_rundll32_suspicious_execution`<br>`T1685.005_event_log_clearing` |
| **silent** | registry_set: 1 of 4 hosts silent (ws03 still sends other events, and none of this kind since 2026-11-06 10:11); the baseline saw about 57 events over the same hours | - | `T1547.001_registry_run_key_persistence` |
| **truncation** | process_creation: command lines are cut at 1024 characters, which the baseline's were not: whatever the rule matches after that length is gone | - | `T1021.006_wsmprovhost_suspicious_child`<br>`T1053.005_powershell_scheduled_task_creation`<br>`T1053.005_schtasks_suspicious_creation`<br>`T1059.001_powershell_encoded_command`<br>`T1218.011_rundll32_suspicious_execution`<br>`T1685.005_event_log_clearing` |
| **delay** | security from dc01: 15% of its events reach the index more than 3 min after they happen (95% within 31 min; the baseline: 19 s): the scheduled search reads each slice 3 min after it closes and never sees them | - | `T1110.003_password_spray_burst`<br>`T1558.003_kerberoasting_volume` |
| **delay** | security from dc01: 15% of its events reach the index more than 5 min after they happen (95% within 31 min; the baseline: 19 s): the scheduled search reads each slice 5 min after it closes and never sees them | - | `T1078.002_honey_account_authentication`<br>`T1558.003_honey_spn_ticket_request`<br>`T1558.003_kerberoasting_rc4_tgs` |
